faq.q: Can this make AI text pass an AI detector?
faq.a: No, and the page says so plainly. It's a rule-based refinement engine, not AI, and it makes no claim about detection tools and cannot 'defeat' any. It's meant for polishing writing you're allowed to edit. Using it to pass off AI-generated work as your own in graded assignments may breach your institution's rules.

faq.q: What specific changes does it suggest?
faq.a: Seven rule types: replacing stock phrases (delve into, it is important to note, furthermore, a plethora of) with simpler alternatives; simplifying nominalisations (utilisation→use); dropping redundant intensifiers (very, really, literally); converting clearly passive 'was X by Y' to active; splitting sentences over 35 words at a conjunction; varying repeated sentence openings; and optionally adding contractions. Each suggestion is listed with the original, the replacement, and why.

faq.q: Do I have to accept every suggested change?
faq.a: No. Every suggestion gets its own checkbox, pre-checked, and you can uncheck any you want to reject then click 'Apply selected', or use 'Accept all' / 'Reject all'. A diff view shows removed text struck through in red and additions highlighted in green, so you can see exactly what each change does before keeping it.

faq.q: How do the tone and contraction settings interact?
faq.a: The Tone menu (Natural, Conversational, Professional) picks which replacement wording is used for stock phrases. The 'Add contractions' toggle only takes effect when the tone is not Professional, so professional output keeps 'it is' and 'do not' spelled out. There's also a 'Vary sentence openings' toggle. The stats panel reports Flesch readability, average sentence length, and sentence-length variation before and after.
